title: Kerala Fish Curry
subtitle: South Indian coconut and tamarind fish curry
excerpt: Kerala fish curry balances sour, coconut, and heat in a way that is unlike any North Indian dish. Tamarind gives it tartness, coconut milk adds sweetness and richness, and the whole thing comes together in under 30 minutes. Use a firm white fish -- it holds together better than flaky varieties.
sourceNotes: Kerala, on India's south-west coast, has one of the longest seafood cooking traditions in the subcontinent. The state is called the land of coconuts, and coconut milk appears in almost every fish preparation. Tamarind and Kodampuli (Malabar tamarind) are the key souring agents.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made 1 day ahead. Add the fish and simmer just before serving.

content.text: Cod holds its shape well here. Haddock or pollock also work. Avoid very thin or flaky fillets as they will break apart. Cut the fish into large chunks -- about 5cm -- so they cook evenly without falling to pieces.

items.prepNote: use a 400ml tin of coconut milk

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 7 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the turmeric and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes, pressing them gently with a spoon until they break down.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind paste. Add the fish sauce and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish pieces. Simmer gently, without stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish is just cooked through. It should flake easily when pressed.
Taste the sauce. Adjust salt and sourness. If you want more tartness, add another teaspoon of tamarind. Serve with boiled rice.

items.cause: Stirred too often or simmered too vigorously
items.fix: Use a gentle simmer and only move the fish once to check doneness

items.cause: Coconut milk needs time to reduce slightly
items.fix: Remove the fish carefully and simmer the sauce for 3 minutes before returning the fish
Add a pinch of sugar and a splash more coconut milk to balance

content.text: Kerala sits on the Malabar Coast and has traded spices with Arabia, China, and Europe for over two thousand years. Fish has always been central to the diet. The sour-coconut balance in this curry reflects that coastal identity. It is eaten for lunch or dinner, always with plain boiled rice to soak up the sauce.
